description: We are PASA UWO, the Physics and Astronomy Student Association from Western University.
summary: Arcadia Pathfinder is a locally hosted web app that computes the safest Mars-walk route between any two points within a region of Arcadia Planitia, Mars. We implement MGS MOLA DEM 463 m topographic data, MGS TES thermal inertia data to synthesize regions of loose soil, buried water ice likelihood (SWIM 2.0), pyroxene exposures (OMEGA), crater rims, close-up HiRISE landing-site photos and CTX imagery. Routes are found with a hazard-aware A* search algorithm on the MOLA DEM grid (cell size 462 x 359 m), and each trip offers Safest, Balanced and Shortest options. Steep ground is penalized (with step cost going to infinity for conditions that exceed safety parameters); users can adjust the slope limit and the penalty scaling for loose ground and crater rims. A “nearest reachable ice” button finds the safest path to water (SWIM 2.0 data). For demonstration and due to data limitations, we restrict the region to the rectangle bounded by (37.5°N, 156°W), (41°N, 171°W), in southern Arcadia and Amazonis Planitia. Within this region are several candidate landing sites studied by SpaceX and NASA JPL. Each route reports distance, climb/descent, peak terrain steepness encountered, integrated loose/dusty ground, and crater rim encounters. ‘3D view’ gives a graphical visualization of the route. This same tool could be applied to any other topographical region.
details:
CONCEPT
Arcadia Pathfinder turns NASA height data into a grid (448 rows by 1,920 columns, about 462 m by 359 m per cell) and finds the lowest-cost route between two points with A* search, running in a background Web Worker so the page stays responsive. Each step costs its distance times a penalty for slope and for hazard layers. Steps steeper than the limit (15° by default, adjustable) are blocked (infinite cost), and cells with no data are avoided. Hazard sliders cover loose or dusty ground (from TES thermal inertia and Dust Cover Index) and crater rims (from the Robbins & Hynek catalogue). A second mode routes to the nearest cell where SWIM 2.0 data says ice is likely within 1 m of the surface. A VR HUD feature is included that can make use of a mobile device's gyroscope to simulate a navigational AR HUD for Mars-walking astronauts.

ROUTES AND OBJECTIVE POINTS
The same search runs with three weightings: Safest (strongest slope and hazard avoidance), Balanced (half the penalties) and Shortest (shortest path that never exceeds the slope limit). They are compared on cards with step-by-step directions using true compass bearings. Objectives are the strongest SWIM 2.0 ice spots, the strongest OMEGA pyroxene spots, a landing site, or a placeable pin anywhere.

DEMO REGION
Southern Arcadia and Amazonis Planitia (37.5°N, 156°W to 41°N, 171°W; about 207 km by 690 km). It includes nine SpaceX Starship candidate sites photographed by HiRISE (S1 to S9), five sites from the NASA/SpaceX study by Golombek et al. (2021), and two HiRISE hazard-study images (P1, P2). We include a field guide with the measured slope, ice score, thermal inertia and dust cover at each site.

OUTPUTS
A 2D map with toggleable layers (including a world map and a Terrain map of shaded relief and contour lines), a 3D view (heights exaggerated 3 to 12 times, with CTX imagery and a low sun), Go and POV route playback, an elevation profile, and a route summary with distance, climb, descent, steepest point and the share of the route on loose ground. Every number shown is measured. Walking times and weather are left out because there are no measured values for them, with one stated exception: the POV “time left” assumes 10 km/h and says so on screen.

EXAMPLE
S1 to S7 with default settings: Safest 341 km (29% loose ground, steepest 8°), Balanced 332 km (41% loose ground, steepest 8°), Shortest 318 km (55% loose ground, steepest 13°).

SAFETY AND HONESTY
The map’s 463 m resolution can’t see boulders, cliffs or small craters, and the ice, dust and thermal inertia cells are coarser (about 3 km), so they mark zones rather than exact spots. “Ice likely” means orbiter data is consistent with ice, not proof. The app states these limits under every route.

TOOLS
JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Vite, Leaflet, Three.js, Chart.js, vite-plugin-pwa (offline/installable), Vitest (19 automated tests of the distance and slope maths and the A* search), and Python with rasterio and NumPy to cut the region from the global MOLA DEM and resample all layers. The finished app is static files with no server.

NEXT STEPS
One cost formula combines slope with several NASA datasets, and users control the trade-off between a shorter route and a safer one. The data script can be rerun on another region (e.g. Gale Crater). Next steps include higher-resolution HiRISE stereo heights for local detail and THEMIS thermal data.

SI USE
We used an SI coding assistant (Claude Code, by Anthropic) to help write the code. The team identified the concept, region, theory, and design, and analyzed the results. This is also stated in the project README.
